brief: Softer PCE readings have pulled some Fed-hike fear out of the market, with October hike odds falling from around 45% to 37%. The note argues the long end is not responding: the 30-year holds near 5.64%, so the dovish repricing at the front end (2-year near 4.89%) has not eased financial conditions further out. The 2s30s spread has re-steepened from roughly 50bp to 75bp, still below August's ~113bp extreme but moving in that direction, showing yields rising faster at the long end than the front. Bond volatility (MOVE near 110 after a recent spike) remains elevated even as equity volatility (VIX near 16) stays contained, a divergence the note flags as equities absorbing the rates shock while bond uncertainty persists. The stated risk: normally weaker growth lowers yields and cushions valuations, but if growth weakens while the long end stays high, equities could see softer earnings without that valuation relief. The note frames the open question as whether the bond market, not the Fed, ultimately responds.
